key_insight: A fast–slow training scheme applies visual token pruning during training so MLLMs process fewer image tokens with little to no accuracy loss, cutting training compute and memory while keeping model quality.
problem_solved: Training multimodal LLMs is inefficient because large numbers of visual tokens inflate compute and memory; prior work reduces model size but not token-related training costs, and naive token pruning during training destabilizes learning.
method: Fast–Slow architecture: a lightweight fast path processes all visual tokens to produce coarse features and pruning scores, while a slow path processes only a retained subset of important tokens with full-capacity layers.

Token selection & schedule: dynamically prune low-importance visual tokens during training using learned scores, with a staged/alternating schedule to preserve gradient signals and representation quality.
Joint optimization: train pruning modules and the backbone end-to-end so the model learns which tokens are essential for downstream multimodal tasks while minimizing training overhead.
impact: This approach lowers training FLOPs and memory for MLLMs, enabling faster pretraining and fine-tuning without large accuracy trade-offs—making multimodal research and deployment more resource-efficient.

paper_title: Fast-Slow Efficient Training for Multimodal Large Language Models via Visual Token Pruning
paper_authors: Dingkun Zhang, Shuhan Qi, Yulin Wu, Xinyu Xiao, Xuan Wang
